title: Customer thread clipboard and engineering anchors
content:
Purpose: quick synthesis of recent customer threads (Feb–Mar 2026) focused on runtime regressions, billing surprises, and low-effort fixes that unblock customers. This is a working clipboard for CS → Eng handoff; not final.

Summary (top-line):
- Recurring theme: three mid-market customers reported increased tail latency when KV-cache warmup is cold after scale events. Impact: degraded interactive experiences for agents and chat.
- Billing anomalies: two customers on Dedicated noticed unexpected token spikes after retries/fallbacks to smaller models. Root cause suspected: retry loop + model-mapping mismatch in routing policy.
- Observability gaps: customers frequently ask for per-request KV-cache hit rates, explicit routing decision traces, and per-model token accounting in the console.

Raw signals and notable excerpts: (notes paraphrased)
- "After we hit a deployment autoscale event, the first ~20 requests have 400–800ms spikes — our UX shows loading states and users abandon." — Enterprise A
- "We saw our bill jump 12% overnight; tracing shows a flurry of retries to a lower-cost model but each retry duplicates token accounting." — Startup B
- "If you could show cache-hit percent on the route dashboard that would make triage 10x faster." — Platform C

Themes (synthesized):
1) Cold-warm transitions and KV cache priming
   - Pattern: autoscale or node failover leads to many cold KV contexts; runtime duplicates work to build KV cache causing latency spikes and increased token emission.
   - Customer impact: interactive agents, chat embeddings with long prefixes, and multimodal sessions.
2) Retry semantics + billing duplication
   - Pattern: fallback/auto-retry path executes a full token generation on a cheaper fallback model while source call already emitted tokens; accounting counts both.
   - Customer impact: surprise spend, loss of trust in per-route cost estimates.
3) Observability and traceability shortfall
   - Pattern: Console lacks easy-to-read breakdowns for cache hits, routing decisions, and per-request model assignments.
   - Customer impact: CS/SREs take 3–4 hours per incident to map behaviour back to infra causes.

Prioritized requests (customer-facing phrasing)
- FR-001: Show per-route KV-cache hit/miss ratio over selectable window (1h/24h/7d) in Redwood Console.
- FR-002: Add a tracing flag that records the routing decision chain (primary → fallback → canary) and surface it in request logs for 90 days.
- FR-003: Prevent double-billing on transparent retries: emit a single unified token accounting event when a retry is logically the same user request.
- FR-004: Provide a runtime config knob: "cache-primer-mode" to aggressively pre-warm KV caches after scale events (configurable cooldown and concurrency limits).
- FR-005: Add an alert template for customers: "KV cache cold-warm spike" (suggested thresholds: p95 latency increase > 200ms and cache-hit < 40%).

Proposed quick mitigations (low effort / high impact)
- QF-1 (platform): Add a lightweight metric export for per-node cache-hit-ratio to existing Prometheus metrics so customers can onboard with dashboards immediately. (est. 1–2w)
- QF-2 (api/runtime): Change retry path to annotate retried requests in the request-log and tie billing events to the idempotency header to dedupe token accounting in billing exports. (est. 2–3w)
- QF-3 (console): Add a temporary UI card on per-route page that surfaces the last 24h sample of routing decisions as a histogram. (est. 1–2w)

Engineering impact and dependencies (notes to eng leads)
- KV cache primer mode requires careful orchestrator hooks: need safe windowing to avoid thundering herd and should be opt-in. Depends: autoscaler events API (infra), runtime cache APIs (serving-runtime). Rough estimate: M work = 3–4 engineer-weeks across infra + runtime.
- Billing dedupe needs changes across API gateway (annotate idempotency), billing pipeline (link events by idempotency + request id), and analytics export. Risk: backward compatibility with existing billing customers. Rough estimate: S–M = 2–6 engineer-weeks with a dedicated billing eng review.

Open questions / unknowns
- Which customers require conservative changes (no opt-in) vs. customers willing to test opt-in primer? We should tag customers who reported issues for early rollout.
- What are safe defaults for primer concurrency? 5 per-model? 20? Need perf tests.
- Is there a way to maintain per-request cost visibility while deduping retries without breaking historical billing?

Customer rollout and communication plan (draft)
- Phase 0: telemetry + logging exports to customers with instructions (week 1–2) — enables immediate visibility.
- Phase 1: opt-in primer mode and routing-debug trace flag for select customers (week 3–6).
- Phase 2: console UI improvements + billing dedupe (week 6–12) — broader rollout tied to billing regression tests.

Action items (owner tags):
- @Priya: assemble list of affected accounts and owners (due: 2026-03-24).
- @Liam: spike on primer-mode perf characteristics and herd protection patterns; produce perf script and results (due: 2026-03-29).
- @Marissa: draft console card mock and minimal schema for routing histograms (due: 2026-03-26).
- @Billing-Eng (Deepak): validate feasibility of idempotency-based billing dedupe and map existing events (due: 2026-04-02).

Notes to CS: When engaging customers, collect simple reproducible steps, timestamps, and an anonymized sample request id. Ask customers to enable debug-trace flag if possible.

Appendix: short reproducer checklist for engs
- Capture traffic around autoscale events (start/stop timestamps).
- Sample full request/response pairs for the cold-warm spike window (including model variant and node id).
- Export billing events for the same window and correlate by request id.

This doc is a living clipboard; add updates below (date-stamped) and keep action items checked in this file.

Updates:
- 2026-03-18: Added Startup B billing spike example after follow-up call; flagged for Billing-Eng review.
- 2026-03-20: Marissa uploaded console mock link to linked_artifacts.

TODOs (short):
- Finalize list of early adopters for primer-mode experiment.
- Create a lightweight Prometheus dashboard template and share with customers.
- Schedule 30m sync (CS + Eng leads + Billing) to align on risks and timeline.

End of clipboard.
